messages:

Subject: Sudden spike in 502/504s for AsteriaLite-3b (production)

Elliot —

We started seeing an uptick in 5xx responses and timeouts against the AsteriaLite-3b model around 08:05 PT this morning. Error rates jumped from ~0.6% to ~6.8% for the /generate endpoint and several requests are timing out (504). Sample trace attached.

Observed: 
- 502 and 504 responses on ~6% of requests (5000 requests/min window)
- Partial payloads returned for some requests
- No changes on our side; traffic steady

We rely on AsteriaLite-3b for low-latency generation. Can you confirm whether there were any deploys or config changes this morning? We need an ETA for mitigation — the increased error rate is affecting several customer-facing flows.

Attachments: request_trace.zip (1.2MB), sample_payloads.json (4KB)

Thanks,
Natalie Cruz

Subject: Internal triage: AsteriaLite-3b 5xx spike (initial findings)

Team —

Triage summary (10:18 PT):
- Timeline: spike began ~08:05 PT; elevated 5xx persisted ~08:05–09:40 and then surfaced again today at ~09:00 in isolated zones.
- Root cause (early signal): a model-serving optimization (kv-cache eviction tuning) rolled into the staging branch yesterday was promoted to canary on a subset of nodes overnight. Canary saw increased cache thrashing at certain sequence-length distributions, which increases cold-start latency and leads to mid-request failures (502) and gateway timeouts (504) when request queues back up.
- Impact: AsteriaLite-3b canonical variant on shared pools; AtlasAI shows concentrated failures in west/us-west region (node group rw-west-pool-4).

Immediate mitigations applied (10:05–10:15 PT):
- Disabled the canary optimization flag on rw-west-pool-4.
- Increased ephemeral pool capacity by +20% in the affected AZ as a short-term relief.
- Adjusted the request queue soft limit to reduce head-of-line blocking (temporary).

Next steps (owners):
- Kimberly: roll back the optimization artifact from canary nodes and verify KV cache behavior (ETA 30–45m).
- Marissa: monitor error rate and perform load verification; prepare rollback manifest for review.
- Elliot: coordinate communication to AtlasAI and offer pinning/dedicated pool options.

I'll post a follow-up when we have the rollback confirmation and pre/post metrics.

Marissa Cole
Senior Operations Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: AsteriaLite-3b — incident closed, summary and postmortem link

Natalie —

Following up with a closure and summary of what we did and next steps. Apologies again for the disruption last week. Short summary:

What happened:
- A canary promotion of a KV-cache eviction tuning change caused cache thrashing under certain request distributions. That increased request latency and pushed some requests into 502/504 failures in the west/us-west pool (rw-west-pool-4).

What we did immediately:
- Disabled the canary optimization and rolled back the artifact from affected nodes (Marissa/Kimberly).
- Temporarily increased pool capacity and adjusted queueing thresholds to reduce head-of-line blocking.
- Routed AtlasAI traffic to the stable model binary (v202604) while we verified stability.

Status and compensation:
- The service is stable for AtlasAI. Error rate has returned to baseline and we have not observed recurrence.
- We will issue a one-time service credit equivalent to 3 days of usage for impacted endpoints. I'll follow up with billing details and a DocuSign for acceptance.

Postmortem and follow-up work:
- RC A doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-asterialite-rca (internal link)
- Action items: strengthen canary isolation, add sequence-length fuzz tests to the canary pipeline, and improve early cache-thrashing alerting (owners: Runtime Reliability).

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute review with our runtime team this week to walk through the RCA and mitigation plan.

Thanks for your patience — please reply if you'd like the pin/dedicated pool while we finish the postmortem actions.

Best,
